claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead measure a generator's expressive range by scoring many outputs on emergent metrics and plotting 2D histograms of the scores.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead require comparison metrics to measure emergent properties of outputs rather than the same parameters used to guide the generator.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: rather than simply using the same parameters that were used

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead say expressive-range analysis can expose unexpected biases in the generation algorithm and holes in the expressive range.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: expose unexpected biases in the generation algorithm and holes

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead measured their own generator Launchpad as clearly biased towards more linear levels.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: The expressive range is clearly biased towards more linear levels

claims.feature: other: sameness traced to one implementation detail
claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead trace Launchpad's linearity bias to a detail that slightly increases the probability of a component appearing again once chosen.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: the probability of that component appearing again is slightly increased

claims.feature: other: sameness traced to one implementation detail
claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead call the linearity bias an unintended side effect of that design decision.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: The linearity bias is an unintended side effect

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead say they would never have realized the far-reaching effect of that minor change without performing the expressive-range analysis.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: we never would have realized such a minor change

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead say design grammars are good at capturing local constraints, and they add global critics to address the resulting over-generation.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: Design grammars are good at capturing local constraints

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead base each expressive-range graph in the paper on 10,000 generated levels unless stated otherwise.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead report that of the 10,000 levels generated, approximately 100 have a good critic measure.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: approximately 100 have a good critic measure

claims.claim: Smith and Whitehead say it is possible for a system to be expressive without necessarily being creative, and decline to call Launchpad creative.
claims.source: Gillian Smith and Jim Whitehead, 'Analyzing the Expressive Range of a Level Generator', PCGames 2010 workshop (ACM), June 2010
claims.quote: possible for a system to be expressive without necessarily being creative

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say there is no logic behind the choice of events in their history generator; events are chosen at random and their texts then profess causes.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: there's no logic behind the choice of events

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew describe cases where the event invents the cause it needs, a full reversal in which the effect causes the cause.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say the sultan's shared state acts as a glue that holds the disjointed generated events together.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: shared state acts as a glue that holds the disjointed events

claims.claim: Grinblat and Bucklew say the assigned domains act as narrative threads that tie together the events of a sultan's life.
claims.source: Jason Grinblat and C. Brian Bucklew, 'Subverting Historical Cause & Effect: Generation of Mythic Biographies in Caves of Qud', FDG'17, Aug 2017
claims.quote: The domains act as narrative threads that tie together the events
